name: Determining the Existence of a Perfect Cuboid

phase_0.domain_name: Determining the Existence of a Perfect Cuboid
phase_0.boundary_condition: the set of four Diophantine equations a^2+b^2=d^2, a^2+c^2=e^2, b^2+c^2=f^2, a^2+b^2+c^2=g^2 with integer variables

VINIT.justification: no integer triple (a,b,c) has been considered; system is uninitialized

TANCH.chosen_element: the perfect cuboid constraints as an object
TANCH.justification: the four equations form a closed boundary that defines the problem

AFWD.chosen_element: generation of a candidate triple (a,b,c) from a parameterization
AFWD.justification: forward transformation from no candidate to a specific integer triple

AREV.chosen_element: infinite descent step: from a perfect cuboid derive a smaller one
AREV.justification: reverse mapping that reduces the size of a solution (if one exists)

CLINK.chosen_element: verification chain: compute squares and check integer square roots
CLINK.justification: sequential composition of arithmetic operations to test the Diphantine conditions

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the set of all perfect cuboids (empty or not) as a self-identical object
IMSCRIB.justification: the problem's identity is invariant under any transformation; it is what it is

FSPLIT.chosen_element: partition of the candidate set by parity of g (space diagonal)
FSPLIT.justification: split the search space into two disjoint subclasses based on whether g is even or odd

FFUSE.chosen_element: union of the two parity subclasses back into the original candidate set
FFUSE.justification: reconstitute the full space from its disjoint partition, reversing the split exactly

EVALT.justification: affirmative branch: the parity condition holds for these candidates

EVALF.justification: negative branch: the parity condition does not hold (i.e., odd) for these candidates

ENGAGR.justification: both existence and non-existence are simultaneously held as unresolved possibilities

IFIX.chosen_element: the result of a non-existence proof (if found) or a verified counterexample
IFIX.justification: irreversible record of a definitive logical conclusion about the problem

phase_2.split_element: partition of the candidate set by parity of g
phase_2.split_input: the full set of integer candidate triples under consideration
phase_2.fuse_element: union of the two parity subsets
phase_2.fuse_result: the original full set of candidate triples (since partition is exhaustive and disjoint)

phase_3.void_description: no candidate triples have been generated or stored; initial emptiness
phase_3.true_description: a candidate triple satisfies all four Diophantine equations (perfect cuboid found)
phase_3.false_description: a candidate triple fails at least one of the four equations
phase_3.both_description: the existence of a perfect cuboid is simultaneously true and false — the problem is open and no proof exists either way

steps.domain_action: establish the empty set of candidate solutions
impose the perfect cuboid constraints as the system boundary
acknowledge that the set of all perfect cuboids (possibly empty) is a fixed self-identical object
partition the search space by the parity of the space diagonal g; even g on T-arm, odd g on F-arm
on the T-arm, consider candidate triples with even g; generate and verify candidates
generate a candidate triple (a,b,c) from a parameterization that yields even g
compute d^2 = a^2+b^2, e^2 = a^2+c^2, f^2 = b^2+c^2, g^2 = a^2+b^2+c^2 and check if all are perfect squares
on the F-arm, consider candidate triples with odd g; generate and verify candidates
generate a candidate triple from a parameterization that yields odd g
perform the same verification chain for the odd-g candidate
combine the results from both parity subclasses; the union of verified perfect cuboids (if any) reconstitutes the full search space
record the overall result — either a perfect cuboid found (permanent counterexample) or a proof of non-existence (descent fixed point)

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the parameterization generator that produces integer triples (a,b,c) satisfying the edge-face diagonal conditions
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: the equality constraints between variables, communicated via shared Diophantine equations
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the set of candidate triples stored for verification
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the order in which parity classes and candidate generations are explored
phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical system of four Pythagorean equations as defined by Euler and later researchers

phase_6.cycle_cost: computational time per candidate triple generation and verification
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: no candidates have been generated or tested
phase_6.post_cycle_state: all relevant candidate triples have been generated and tested (or a descent proof has been applied)
